The four hits the broad sweep returns are a reprint of Senator Ewing's Post Office report (1834-09-24 page 3 column 1 line 2717), a Cumberland postmaster's letter about mail robbers (1834-09-10 page 3 column 1 lines 2382-2393), the Postmaster General's own Chicago-to-Green-Bay proposals (1834-09-17 page 3 column 3 lines 2807-2822, extracted as `infrastructure`) and a want-advertisement routing replies through the post office (1834-09-03 page 3 column 3 lines 3109-3118). The survey T-0291 was written against is therefore confirmed by reading rather than trusted: the epic's letter-list ruling has nothing to bite on in September 1834, and the hand count the ticket asks for is a count of zero printed lists against zero extracted. AGREES WITH T-0290 next door: August 1834 carries no Chicago list either, the town's 1 July return having been withdrawn in mid-July.

Vol. I Nos. 44-48, 1834-10-01 to 1834-10-29. Five issues, read through. THE MONTH'S LETTER LIST IS THE 1 OCTOBER 1834 CHICAGO LIST and it is printed three times — 1834-10-08 page 3 columns 1-2, 1834-10-15 page 3 columns 2-3, and 1834-10-22 page 1 columns 1-2. It is minted ONCE, from 1834-10-22, which is the only witness that carries it whole; the other two printings are recorded as reprints with their names unminted, so one list makes one cohort of people (T-0299). 1834-10-01 and 1834-10-29 carry no Chicago list — the latter prints the Hennepin and Plainfield ones, which are recorded and not minted, as are the Du Page and Plainfield lists under the Chicago one on 1834-10-22.

The scene-date issue, read through. Declared as a one-day range because that is exactly what was read: T-0296 declares 8 to 29 July when it reads them, T-0297 August, T-0298 January to June. A range is a promise the gate keeps, so it is only widened by the pass that widens the reading.

Vol. I Nos. 7-10, 1834-01-07 to 1834-01-28. Four issues, read through. Their transcriptions are deposit-held, so the quotes were machine-checked with `--check --deposit <path>` against a read-only copy of the deposit from `main`; on `dev` their claims are counted unresolved and reported, which is green (T-0275). THE LETTER LIST: the post office at Chicago's list of 1 January 1834 is printed twice in the month — cut to a handful of names on 1834-01-14 and nearly whole on 1834-01-28 — and the residents are minted from the second, where 97 names and the postmaster's signature survive. Ninety-seven is a FLOOR and not the printed length: the .docx extraction crushed the list's two alphabetical columns into eight paragraph lines and left orphan debris where names stood. The gap is a ticket, not an estimate.

Vol. I Nos. 2-6, 1833-12-03 to 1833-12-31. Five issues, read through. Their transcriptions are deposit-held, so the quotes were machine-checked with `--check --deposit <path>` against a read-only copy of the deposit from `main`; on `dev` their claims are counted unresolved and reported, which is green (T-0275). THE MONTH CARRIES NO POST-OFFICE LETTER LIST. Swept all five issues for every form the Democrat uses — 'list of letters', 'letters remaining', 'remaining in the post office', 'uncalled for', a signature ending 'P. M.', and the bare words 'post office' and 'postmaster' — for hits in every issue and not one of them a list: they are the paper's OWN agent list on page 1, which names eight out-of-county postmasters (George Cloud of America, Elijah Willard of Jonesboro', Daniel Converse of Waterloo and so on) and is reprinted unchanged in all five numbers, plus two national paragraphs about the Post Master General (1833-12-17) and the Postmaster of New-York (1833-12-24), plus J. Bates jr.'s standing advertisement asking enquirers to call at the P. Office. The hand count the ticket asks for is therefore ZERO printed lists against ZERO extracted names, and it agrees with T-0308 next door: No. 1 of 1833-11-26 carries none either. The Chicago post office's own list does not appear in this corpus until 1 January 1834, printed cut on 1834-01-14 and nearly whole on 1834-01-28 (T-0310). THE MONTH'S PRINCIPAL DOCUMENT IS THE WHARFING ORDINANCE of 4 December 1833 — sections 11-16 adopted at the house of Dexter Graves, printed first on 1833-12-10 and legibly on 1833-12-24, minted once from the second, on T-0292's one-printing-one-claim discipline. THE DIALECT CHANGES INSIDE THE RANGE: Nos. 2-5 are dash-column and No. 6 is the prose `Newspaper Page` / `Column` pair, and No. 2 carries the BARE `SOURCE PDF PAGE n` banner, whose pages the resolver counts ordinally because the scan page is not the issue page (this issue opens at scan page 5). THE ORDINANCE WAS ALREADY IN THE CORPUS FROM ITS JANUARY REPRINT: T-0310 read sections 11, 13, 14 and 15 off 1834-01-07 before these December printings were read. Those claims stand; the December ones are kept beside them because they are the SENIOR witnesses — first printing on 1833-12-10, clearest on 1833-12-24 — and because each carries text the January reprint lost: the four names of the bridge committee and the word REPAIRING, the whole of the eighty-feet and fifteen-dollar clauses, the whole of section 16, and the president's and clerk's signatures. Each of the seven December ordinance claims names its January counterpart in its own notes.

Vol. I Nos. 18-22, 1834-04-01 to 1834-04-30. Five issues, read through, 71 claims. Their transcriptions are deposit-held, so the quotes were machine-checked with `--check --deposit <path>` against a read-only copy of the deposit from `main`; on `dev` their claims are counted unresolved and reported, which is green (T-0275). THE MONTH'S LETTER LIST IS THE 1 APRIL 1834 CHICAGO LIST, AND NOBODY KNEW IT WAS THERE. `data/research/newspapers/README.md` said in as many words that of T-0258's thirty issues only 1834-01-28, 1834-02-04, 1834-04-23 and 1834-04-30 carry a list, and T-0313's own brief repeated it as 'TWO letter lists (1834-04-23 and 1834-04-30)'. Both are wrong twice over. The two April lists that sweep found are the HENNEPIN list, printed three times in this month (1834-04-16 page 3 column 4, 1834-04-23 page 3 column 5, 1834-04-30 page 3 column 5) and recorded here without minting a name, as T-0290 and T-0292 treated the Hennepin and Plainfield lists before it. Chicago's own list of letters remaining on 1 April 1834, over J. S. C. Hogan's signature, is printed TWICE in the issues the sweep passed over — 1834-04-01 page 3 columns 3 and 4, and again 1834-04-08 page 3 columns 3 and 4. WHY EVERY SWEEP MISSED IT: the heading on 1834-04-01 reads `SQA AINIG init`, which is REMAINING, and the words `List of Letters` stand in the NEXT segmenter column over the list's second half; so a search for 'list of letters', 'letters remaining', 'remaining in the post office', 'uncalled for' or a signature ending 'P. M.' finds the Hennepin list in this month and not the Chicago one. It is minted ONCE (T-0292's rule, T-0299's complaint), from 1834-04-01: 163 names there, plus 16 names from the 1834-04-08 reprint that the first printing's transcription crushed and nothing else from that reprint, for 179 in one cohort. 179 IS A FLOOR AND NOT THE PRINTED LENGTH — nineteen lines across the two printings carry debris where a name stood and are left unread rather than guessed at, and the page-image pass that would close the gap is T-0321, filed with this run. The month also carries what a reconstruction can actually use: the Board of Trustees' order of 5 March 1834 for a ten-foot plank or brick sidewalk with two-inch oak curbing along South Water Street, made at the house of Dexter Graves; John H. Kinzie's ware house opposite Fort Dearborn; a boot and shoe shop next door to P. Cohen's store; a dwelling house on lot 3 of block 18 and a store room in the rear of J. B. Beaubien's store house; and, on 1834-04-16, the sentence `Seven or eight buildings have been raised in this town within the past week`. TRANSCRIPTION QUALITY IS THE WORST IN THE RANGE SO FAR: 75 of the month's 160 segmenter columns carry the Tesseract fallback banner and they are concentrated on pages 3 and 4, where the town is.

Vol. I Nos. 11-14, 1834-02-04 to 1834-02-25. Four issues, read through. Their transcriptions are deposit-held, so the quotes were machine-checked with `--check --deposit <path>` against a read-only copy of the deposit from `main`; on `dev` their claims are counted unresolved and reported, which is green (T-0275). THE MONTH'S LETTER LIST IS THE 1 JANUARY 1834 CHICAGO LIST IN ITS THIRD PRINTING, at 1834-02-04 page 4 column 2, and IT IS THE BEST WITNESS THE CORPUS HOLDS TO THAT LIST. It is NOT minted: T-0310 already minted 97 residents from the printing of 1834-01-28, and T-0292's rule for a list printed more than once — mint once, record the reprints — is the rule T-0299 exists because July 1834 broke. The reading is made in full in the claim's `normalized` field instead. THE COUNT, stated against the printing as the ticket asks: 71 names survive at name level in the first alphabetical column, A to H, Atkins to Harkness, with four further lines of that column reduced to debris, so the printed first column was about 75 names. T-0310 minted 97 from the WHOLE list; ~75 in the A-H half alone confirms that ninety-seven is a floor and not the printed length, which T-0310's note asserted and this pass measures. This printing also REFUTES T-0318's premise that 'the images are the only route' — it is in the ruled dialect, one name per line, and repairs the A-H half at the transcription: 'William Cr[…]' is William Criss. T-0323 carries that. A SECOND letter list runs in the same issue, from an out-of-county office signed by Thomas Calaher and not by J. S. C. Hogan; it is recorded and not minted, as T-0292 recorded the Hennepin and Plainfield lists. Swept all four issues for every form the Democrat uses — 'list of letters', 'letters remaining', 'remaining in the post office', 'uncalled for', a signature ending 'P. M.' — for these two lists and, at 1834-02-11, the postmaster's own mail timetable, which is extracted as `infrastructure`.
